free_tier.stated: Each project in a Free tier namespace on GitLab.com has 10 GiB of free storage.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: The default limit is 52428800 bytes (50 MB).
per_object_cap.notes: The first-party administration page states a 52428800-byte (50 MB) default snippet size cap; the admin snippet page also states the same limit in bytes.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No expiry or deletion term is stated for project or snippet objects; an over-quota project is set read-only, which rejects pushes without deleting content. Explicitly deleted projects are permanently removed after a 30-day delay.

egress.terms: unmetered, served from gitlab.com; no egress line item exists on any GitLab.com plan.

tooling: Glab CLI (glab snippet create), VS Code extension, REST /api/v4/snippets, plain git clone/push for project repos. rclone has a 'gitlab' backend (yes — rclone supports GitLab as a Git remote type via backend 'git').
chaining: Free accounts permit multiple projects at 10 GiB git storage each. Snippets provide a standalone 50 MB per object upload mechanism outside of project repositories.
limits_note: 10 GiB per project then the project goes read-only (pushes rejected) until storage is purchased. A hard stop, not a warning; 50 MB per snippet; namespace storage updated every 90 minutes; 5 GiB per-file push limit on gitlab.com is not documented publicly, so shard files.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Read-only lockout is automatic and immediate on exceeding 10 GiB, and it blocks pushes rather than deletes data. Snippets are counted in namespace storage, so they are not a separate free pool.
confidence_note: the administration snippets page states the default snippet size limit is 52428800 bytes (50 MB)
